ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AD=DC$. If $\angle BAD=20^\circ$, find the degree measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Given the problem, \\
$\because DA=DC$, \\
$\therefore \angle DAC=\angle C$, \\
$\because \angle ADB$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ADC$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADB=\angle DAC+\angle C=2\angle C$, \\
$\because AB=AD$, \\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle ADB=2\angle C$, \\
$\because \angle B+\angle ADB+\angle BAD=180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore 2\angle C+20^\circ+2\angle C=180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle C=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, B, D, C are on the same horizontal base, D is between B and C, and an internal line segment AD is drawn from A to D. The problem gives AB = AD = DC, and ∠BAD = 20°. Reasoning: Let x = ∠C. Since D is on BC, ∠C = ∠ACD = x. Because AD = DC, triangle ADC is an isosceles triangle, the base angles are equal, obtaining ∠DAC = ∠ACD = x. Since DB is the extension of DC, ∠ADB is the exterior angle of triangle ADC at point D, therefore ∠ADB = ∠DAC + ∠ACD = x + x = 2x. Also because AB = AD, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 2x. In triangle ABD, ∠BAD + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°, that is 20° + 2x + 2x = 180°. So 4x = 160°, x = 40°. Final answer: ∠C = 40°.
